items.title: 11,952 violators of residency, labor and border security laws arrested in a week
items.title_zh: 一周内有11952名违反居留、劳工和边境安全法的人被逮捕
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi security forces arrested a total of 11,952 illegal residents in a week. The arrests were made in joint inspections, carried out in cooperation with the relevant government agencies, during the period between November 5 and 11, the Ministry of Interior announced on Saturday. Those who were arrested include 6,163 violators of the Residency Law, 3,225 violators of the Border Security Law, and 2,564 violators of the Labor Law. The total number of people who were arrested while trying to cross the border into the Kingdom accounted for 1,653. About 29 people were arrested while attempting to leave the Kingdom illegally.A total of 11,418 illegal residents were deported while 22,451 violators were referred to their diplomatic missions to obtain travel documents and 9,800 violators were referred to complete their travel reservations. Fifteen persons, who were involved in giving transportation, shelter, and employment for violators, were also arrested. A total of 40,762 expatriates, including 38,383 men and 2,379 women, are currently undergoing procedures to enforce legal measures for their violations. The Ministry of Interior has warned that any person, who facilitates the illegal entry of individuals into the Kingdom, transports them on its territory, provides them with shelter or any other assistance or service, will be penalized with up to 15 years in prison and a fine of up to SR1 million, and that the vehicles used for transportation or houses used for giving shelter will be confiscated. The ministry urged the public to report any cases of violation by calling the number 911 in the regions of Makkah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province and the numbers 999 and 996 in the rest of the Kingdom’s regions.

items.title: Arab, Islamic FMs slam Israeli strike on Gaza’s Nasser Medical Complex, demand unhindered aid delivery
items.title_zh: 阿拉伯和伊斯兰国家外长谴责以色列对加沙纳赛尔医疗中心的袭击，要求不受阻碍地运送援助物资
items.summary: RIYADH — The foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and several other Arab and Islamic countries condemned in the strongest terms the Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, which caused casualties among patients and medical personnel. In a joint statement, they reiterated that the attack is in flagrant violation of international humanitarian law, which affords special protection to medical facilities and healthcare workers.The foreign ministers also include those from the countries of Egypt, Türkiye, Pakistan, Indonesia, Sudan, Libya, Palestine, Djibouti, Somalia, Oman, Mauritania, Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Lebanon, and Algeria. They also denounced continued Israeli attacks on Palestinian civilians, including strikes on tents and other sites sheltering displaced persons. These attacks undermine the ceasefire and efforts to restore security and stability in Gaza and are inconsistent with President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan. The ministers expressed grave concern that continued Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid, shelter materials, including tents, caravans and mobile homes, as well as medical supplies are deepening Gaza's humanitarian catastrophe as winter approaches. Inadequate shelter and deteriorating water, sanitation and healthcare services put civilian lives at grave risk, particularly those of children and infants, who could once again die from exposure to freezing temperatures. The ministers called on Israel to heed appeals from the international community and the Board of Peace, for increased aid and to fulfil immediately and in full its obligations under the Sharm El-Sheikh Agreement, President Trump's Comprehensive Plan and United Nations Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025). Israel must uphold the ceasefire, protect civilians and medical facilities, and ensure the safe, sustained and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian aid in sufficient quantities, including shelter and early recovery supplies and equipment to restore essential infrastructure. It must also allow United Nations agencies and humanitarian organizations to carry out their mandates without obstruction. These first-phase commitments were due to take effect upon signature. Israel must implement them without further delay or additional conditions, including political and security conditions, that impede humanitarian access. Urgent humanitarian assistance must proceed independently of progress on subsequent phases. The ministers called on the United States and the Board of Peace, within their respective roles, to intensify their efforts to ensure Israel's full implementation of these commitments and the lifting of all restrictions on the entry of humanitarian aid, thereby preserving the credibility of the agreements and consolidating the ceasefire. The ministers reaffirmed their determination to work with regional and international partners to consolidate the ceasefire, implement all phases of the plan and scale up humanitarian assistance to alleviate the suffering of the Palestinian people.

items.title: Saudi, US housing ministers discuss cooperation in urban planning, property finance
items.title_zh: 沙特与美国住房部长讨论城市规划和房地产融资方面的合作
items.summary: VIRGINIA — Minister of Municipalities and Housing Majed Al-Hogail discussed with US Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Scott Turner expanding bilateral cooperation between Saudi Arabia and the United States in housing, urban planning, and real estate finance. The meeting was held on the sidelines of the Ginnie Mae 2026 Global Investor Summit on Financing Affordable Housing in Virginia, the United States. The ministers reviewed ways to leverage regulatory and operational expertise to boost housing supply and incentivize private-sector investment, alongside developing real estate finance instruments and enhancing integration between housing authorities and financial institutions to improve market efficiency and broaden homeownership options for families.The meeting also addressed establishing an institutional framework for technical cooperation, expertise exchange, and reciprocal visits to facilitate knowledge transfer and foster new partnerships between Saudi and American institutions in advancing housing and financial solutions.Addressing the summit, Al-Hogail said that Saudi Arabia is actively developing its housing finance sector and linking real estate lending to long-term capital markets to bolster market sustainability and broaden affordable housing options. “The Saudi Real Estate Refinance Company (SRC) aims to refinance more than $40 billion by 2030. The initiative opens significant avenues for international investors to participate in Saudi fixed-income instruments and real estate securities, while fostering collaboration in securitisation, guarantees, data management, and modern credit risk technologies,” he said. The minister emphasized that the Kingdom offers a robust market underpinned by sustained, long-term housing demand. He noted that financing, guarantee, and servicing tools are being developed within a transparent regulatory framework supervised by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) and the Capital Market Authority (CMA). He urged global investors to partner in building a market that serves families while generating sustainable returns.

items.title: Ministry of Hajj and Umrah completes signing of agreements for 2027 Hajj season
items.title_zh: 朝觐与副朝事务部完成2027年朝觐季协议的签署
items.summary: JEDDAH — The Ministry of Hajj and Umrah has completed the signing of Hajj arrangement agreements for the 2027 season with Hajj affairs offices, in preparation for the upcoming Hajj season.The agreements were signed by Minister of Hajj and Umrah Tawfiq Al-Rabiah, Deputy Minister of Hajj and Umrah Dr. Abdulfattah Mashat, and heads of Hajj affairs offices from participating countries on the sidelines of the sixth Hajj Conference and Exhibition, which concluded in Jeddah onWednesday.The agreements outline coordination mechanisms between the ministry and Hajj affairs offices, approved requirements and procedures for the season, and the responsibilities and obligations of the parties regarding services provided to pilgrims and arrangements for their arrival and departure.The signing of the agreements follows the ministry-provided preparatory document sent to Hajj affairs offices at the end of the 2026 Hajj season to begin preparations for the upcoming season, which allows the offices to complete contracts and regulatory, operational, and service requirements early.Preparations also included signing agreements on pilgrim dispatching preferences to organize the movement of pilgrims, and completing the documentation of contracts signed with airlines through the e-Path platform within the specified deadlines.

items.title: ZATCA foils attempt to smuggle 413,450 amphetamine pills at Al-Haditha Port
items.title_zh: ZATCA挫败了在哈迪萨港走私413,450粒安非他明药片的企图
items.summary: RIYADH — Al-Haditha Customs has foiled an attempt to smuggle 413,450 amphetamine pills into the Kingdom, discovering the narcotics concealed within a commercial shipment arriving through the northern land port. Spokesperson of the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) Hamoud Al-Harbi stated that during standard inspection procedures of an incoming truck at Al-Haditha port, officers uncovered the pills hidden inside a consignment of canned fava beans. Al-Harbi affirmed that ZATCA continues to enforce strict customs oversight across all land, sea, and air ports to safeguard society and counter smuggling attempts, working in close coordination with the Ministry of Interior and the General Directorate of Narcotics Control. He also called on the public to support anti-smuggling efforts and protect society and the national economy by reporting smuggling crimes or violations of the Unified Customs Law via the dedicated security hotline 1910, the international number 009661910, or by email 1910@zatca.gov.sa. “All reports are treated with strict confidentiality and whistleblowers receive financial rewards for verified information,” he added.

items.title: Arab Parliament welcomes UN resolution demanding immediate halt to Houthi attacks
items.title_zh: 阿拉伯议会欢迎联合国决议，要求立即停止胡塞武装的袭击
items.summary: CAIRO — The Arab Parliament has welcomed UN Security Council Resolution 2837, which demands that the Houthi militia immediately halt its military escalation and attacks, including those targeting Saudi Arabia, civilians, commercial airports and international maritime transport. In a statement issued on Friday, the parliament said the resolution’s unanimous adoption reflects growing international recognition of the seriousness of Houthi activities and their implications for regional security, stability and freedom of international navigation. The parliament described the resolution as an important step toward unifying international opposition to the militia’s terrorist acts and continued violations. It stressed the need to translate international condemnations into decisive, practical measures to halt the attacks and hold those responsible accountable. The parliament also welcomed the extension of the sanctions regime imposed on entities linked to the Houthi militia, to prevent activities threatening the security and stability of Yemen and the wider region. It reaffirmed its support for efforts to enable Yemen’s legitimate government to exercise its constitutional responsibilities, preserve the country’s unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity, and fulfill the Yemeni people’s aspirations for security, stability, peace and development. The Arab Parliament stressed that a comprehensive political solution remains the only path to ending the Yemeni crisis.

items.title: Jordan, Egypt, Kuwait, Bahrain and Arab League condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.title_zh: 约旦、埃及、科威特、巴林和阿拉伯国家联盟谴责胡塞武装对沙特阿拉伯的袭击
items.summary: RIYADH — Jordan, Egypt, Kuwait, Bahrain and the Arab League have strongly condemned the terrorist Houthi militia’s continued missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their solidarity with the Kingdom and support for measures taken to protect its security and sovereignty. In a statement issued on Thursday, Jordan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the continued attacks, most recently involving the launch of two ballistic missiles toward the Makkah region, along with missiles and drones directed at Riyadh and other areas of the Kingdom. The ministry described the attacks as flagrant violations of Saudi sovereignty, international law and the UN Charter, reaffirming Jordan’s rejection of attacks targeting civilians and civilian and economic infrastructure. Jordan also reiterated its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for measures taken to protect its security, stability, sovereignty, national assets, citizens and residents. Meanwhile, the Arab League strongly condemned the launch of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones toward Makkah,Riyadh and Saudi Arabia’s eastern and southern regions, describing the attacks as a dangerous escalation threatening the Kingdom’s security and civilian lives. The organization stressed that targeting Saudi territory, particularly areas housing Islamic holy sites, violates the Kingdom’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, international law and the UN Charter, while infringing upon the sanctity of religious sites and provoking Muslims worldwide. The Arab League praised the effectiveness of Saudi air defenses in intercepting and thwarting the attacks and reaffirmed its support for the Kingdom’s legitimate measures to protect its territory, citizens and residents. It also warned that continued attacks would heighten regional tensions and undermine de-escalation efforts, urging the international community, particularly the UN Security Council, to ensure the implementation of relevant resolutions, including 2216 (2015) and 2817 (2026). Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs also condemned the continued attacks on Saudi territory, most recently involving ballistic missiles and drones launched toward Makkah, describing them as violations of Saudi sovereignty, international law and the UN Charter. The ministry warned that the attacks directly threaten civilians and civilian and economic facilities while undermining regional security and stability. Egypt reaffirmed its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for measures taken to protect its security, sovereignty, territorial integrity and national assets, stressing that the Kingdom’s security is an integral part of Egyptian and Arab national security. Kuwait’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs similarly condemned the continued Houthi attacks using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones against several Saudi regions, describing them as repeated terrorist attacks that violate Saudi sovereignty, international law and international humanitarian law. The ministry rejected the attacks, warning that they threaten civilian safety and undermine regional stability. Kuwait reiterated its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for measures taken to safeguard its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity, emphasizing that the Kingdom’s security is inseparable from Kuwait’s security and that of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states. Bahrain’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs also strongly condemned the continued Houthi attacks involving ballistic missiles and drones directed toward Makkah, Riyadh and Saudi Arabia’s eastern and southern regions. The ministry described the attacks as a dangerous escalation following the targeting of Madinah region days earlier, which resulted in missile fragments falling in populated areas. Bahrain stressed that the attacks violate Saudi sovereignty, international law and international humanitarian law, threaten civilian lives and infringe upon the sanctity of Islamic holy sites. The ministry praised the Royal Saudi Air Defense Forces for intercepting and thwarting the attacks, reaffirming Bahrain’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for measures taken to protect its security, sovereignty, citizens and residents. It also emphasized the Kingdom’s legitimate right to self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, stressing that Saudi security is inseparable from Bahrain’s security and the broader GCC security framework. Bahrain renewed its call for the UN Security Council to take firm action to halt repeated Houthi attacks, prevent the targeting of religious holy sites and civilian facilities, hold perpetrators and their supporters accountable, and ensure the implementation of relevant Security Council resolutions.
